availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

availableCommands.name: agents-sdk
availableCommands.description: Build AI agents on Cloudflare Workers using the Agents SDK. Load when creating stateful agents, durable workflows, real-time WebSocket apps, scheduled tasks, MCP servers, chat applications, voice agents, or browser automation. Covers Agent class, state management, callable RPC, Workflows, durable execution, queues, retries, observability, and React hooks. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive Cloudflare platform skill covering Workers, Pages, storage (KV, D1, R2), AI (Workers AI, Vectorize, Agents SDK), feature flags (Flagship), networking (Tunnel, Spectrum), security (WAF, DDoS), and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi). Use for any Cloudflare development task. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-email-service
availableCommands.description: Send and receive transactional emails with Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending + Email Routing). Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Even for simple requests like "add email to my Worker" — this skill has critical config details.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-one
availableCommands.description: Guides Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE work across Access, Gateway, WARP, Tunnel, Cloudflare WAN, DLP, CASB, device posture, and identity. Use when designing, configuring, troubleshooting, or reviewing Cloudflare One deployments. Retrieval-first: use current Cloudflare docs/API schemas instead of embedded product docs.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-one-migrations
availableCommands.description: Plans migrations from Zscaler ZIA/ZPA, Palo Alto, legacy VPN, SWG, or SASE stacks to Cloudflare One. Use for migration assessments, policy mapping, rollout plans, and parity/gap analysis.

availableCommands.name: durable-objects
availableCommands.description: Create and review Cloudflare Durable Objects. Use when building stateful coordination (chat rooms, multiplayer games, booking systems), implementing RPC methods, SQLite storage, alarms, WebSockets, or reviewing DO code for best practices. Covers Workers integration, wrangler config, and testing with Vitest. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: reverse-engineering

availableCommands.name: sandbox-sdk
availableCommands.description: Build sandboxed applications for secure code execution. Load when building AI code execution, code interpreters, CI/CD systems, interactive dev environments, or executing untrusted code. Covers Sandbox SDK lifecycle, commands, files, code interpreter, and preview URLs. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: turnstile-spin
availableCommands.description: Set up Cloudflare Turnstile end-to-end in a project — scan the codebase, create the widget via the Cloudflare API, deploy the managed siteverify Worker, write the frontend snippets, validate, and persist the skill. Load this when a user asks to add Turnstile, set up CAPTCHA, protect a form from bots, or fix a Turnstile integration. Mirrors developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/spin.

availableCommands.name: web-perf
availableCommands.description: Analyzes web performance using Chrome DevTools MCP. Measures Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) and supplementary metrics (FCP, TBT, Speed Index), identifies render-blocking resources, network dependency chains, layout shifts, caching issues, and accessibility gaps. Use when asked to audit, profile, debug, or optimize page load performance, Lighthouse scores, or site speed. Biases towards retrieval from current documentation over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: workers-best-practices
availableCommands.description: Reviews and authors Cloudflare Workers code against production best practices. Load when writing new Workers, reviewing Worker code, configuring wrangler.jsonc, or checking for common Workers anti-patterns (streaming, floating promises, global state, secrets, bindings, observability). Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

Load before running wrangler commands to ensure correct syntax and best practices. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

---
name: ghostwire-builder
description: Implements GhostWire spec tasks in C# (.NET 8) and vanilla JavaScript with minimal changes, then runs the test harness.
tools: ["read", "write", "shell"]
resources:
  - file://README.md
  - file://.kiro/steering/**/*.md
permissions:
  rules:
    - capability: shell
      match: ["tools/dotnet *", "git status*", "git diff*"]
      effect: allow
    - capability: shell
      match: ["git push*", "rm -rf*"]
      effect: deny
---

You implement tasks for GhostWire, a simulation-only OT Security & Troubleshooting Lab (ASP.NET Core C# on .NET 8, plain HTML/CSS/JS frontend). Follow the steering files in your resources, especially safety.md.

## How you work

1. Read the spec task you were given (`.kiro/specs/<feature>/tasks.md`) and the requirements and design it refers to. Do only that task. If the task is unclear or conflicts with safety.md, stop and ask.
2. Read the code you will change before editing it. Follow its existing style.
3. Make the smallest change that completes the task. No unrelated refactors, renames or formatting changes.
4. After every set of edits, run from the repository root:
   `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj`
   Use `tools/dotnet`, never bare `dotnet`, because the repository is on `/mnt/d` and the wrapper calls Windows `dotnet.exe`. Fix failures before you report.
5. Report: the files changed, what each change does, the test command and its actual result. Mark the task done only if the tests passed.

## Rules

- Never add a NuGet package, npm package or other dependency without asking first.
- Never add a request field, setting or environment variable that selects a Modbus host, port or arbitrary URL. Connect only to `IPAddress.Loopback` and simulator-owned ports.
- Learner-facing code never sends Modbus writes. Phantom Writer's FC06 exists only inside the simulator.
- Do not invent protocol results in UI text, tests or docs. Show only what the simulator returned.
- Do not commit, push or delete directories. Leave version control to the owner.

</content>
</file>

<file name=".kiro/specs/ot-security-lab/requirements.md" language="markdown" >
<content>
# Requirements Document: ot-security-lab

## Introduction

This feature extends GhostWire from a three-case Modbus troubleshooting lab into an OT security and troubleshooting lab. It adds:

- a frame inspector that shows the actual Modbus TCP bytes of every simulated read;
- a defensive incident case, **Phantom Writer**, in which the learner finds an unauthorized FC06 write in a simulated captured traffic log;
- case categories and difficulty;
- property-based tests in the existing dependency-free harness;
- updated judge documentation for all four cases.

The existing cases (The Giant Pressure, The Silent Sensor, The Wrong Register) keep their behavior. Existing API fields keep their names, types and meaning. Every value shown to a learner comes from a simulator run on loopback. Nothing in this feature connects to physical equipment, lets a learner send a Modbus write, or claims anything about a real installation.

The steering files `.kiro/steering/{product,safety,tech,modbus-protocol,accessibility}.md` apply to every requirement below.

## Glossary

- **ADU**: Modbus TCP application data unit. The 7-byte MBAP header followed by the PDU.
- **MBAP header**: Modbus Application Protocol header: transaction ID (2 bytes), protocol ID (2), length (2), unit ID (1).
- **PDU**: Protocol data unit. Function code (1 byte) followed by function-specific data.
- **FC03 / FC04 / FC06**: Read Holding Registers / Read Input Registers / Write Single Register.
- **Frame**: The exact bytes of one ADU sent or received on a loopback TCP connection.
- **Frame inspector**: The "Wire evidence" panel and the `frames` field that expose frames and their decoded fields.
- **Learner read path**: `POST /api/test` and the `ModbusClient` code it calls.
- **Incident generator**: Server-side startup code that performs the scripted Phantom Writer exchanges against its own private simulator and records them.
- **Traffic log**: The simulated captured traffic produced by the incident generator.
- **Client label**: A simulated name (for example `HMI-01`) that the incident generator assigns to each of its own TCP connections. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity; the label is capture metadata.
- **Evidence categories**: `observations`, `possible_causes`, `training_hints`, `next_steps`, `verified`.
- **Property**: A statement that must hold for every generated input in a property-based test.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: Frame inspector

**User Story:** As a learner, I want to see the exact Modbus TCP bytes of each simulated read and what each byte means, so that I can check my request and the device's reply from wire evidence instead of from a summary.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN `POST /api/test` completes with status `response`, `exception` or `error`, THE SYSTEM SHALL include a `frames` array in the result containing one request frame and, if any response bytes were received, one response frame.
2. WHEN `POST /api/test` completes with status `timeout`, THE SYSTEM SHALL include only the request frame in `frames`.
3. IF the request bytes were not fully written to the socket (for example the loopback connection failed), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return an empty `frames` array and SHALL NOT show a request frame that was never transmitted.
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL represent each frame as `{ "direction": "request" | "response", "hex": string, "fields": [ { "name", "value", "bytes" } ], "decode_error": string | null }`, where `hex` is the uppercase, space-separated hexadecimal form of the bytes and `bytes` is `{ "offset": int, "length": int }` into that frame.
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL build `hex` from the byte arrays actually written to and read from the loopback socket, not by re-encoding the request settings.
6. WHEN a frame is decoded, THE SYSTEM SHALL list these fields in byte order: transaction ID, protocol ID, length, unit ID, function code, then for an FC03/FC04 request the start address and quantity; for an FC03/FC04 response the byte count and one field per register value; for an FC06 request or response the register address and register value; for an exception response the exception code.
7. IF a response frame cannot be fully decoded (wrong protocol ID, length outside 2–254, byte count mismatch or truncated data), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return the fields decoded so far and a non-null `decode_error` describing the first failure, and SHALL NOT throw.
8. WHEN a result is rendered, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the frames in a collapsible panel titled "Wire evidence", collapsed by default, labeled as simulated.
9. THE SYSTEM SHALL render each frame as a `<table>` with header cells for field name, bytes (hex, monospace) and decoded value, and SHALL define MBAP, PDU, unit ID and function code in plain language the first time the panel shows them.
10. WHEN a learner hovers over or moves keyboard focus to a field row, THE SYSTEM SHALL highlight the matching bytes in the frame's hex display and SHALL indicate the link in text (byte offset and length), not by color alone.
11. THE SYSTEM SHALL make the panel and every field row reachable and operable with the keyboard alone, and SHALL respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Requirement 2: Phantom Writer incident case

**User Story:** As a learner, I want to investigate a simulated unauthorized setpoint change from a captured traffic log, so that I can practice identifying a Modbus write from evidence and learn which real-world controls reduce that risk.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SYSTEM SHALL provide a scenario with id `phantom-writer`, title "Phantom Writer" and category `security`, whose simulated device is a boiler controller at unit ID 5 with holding register offset 100 holding the temperature setpoint at 0.1 °C per count, documented normal value 650 (65.0 °C).
2. WHEN the server starts, THE SYSTEM SHALL generate the traffic log by performing real Modbus TCP exchanges over loopback between the incident generator and a private, write-enabled simulator that no HTTP endpoint can reach.
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a traffic log of 12 transactions: 11 FC03 reads of holding register 100 from client label `HMI-01`, and one FC06 write of value 950 to register 100 from a different client label, at a fixed position in the sequence.
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL make the traffic log deterministic: client labels, transaction IDs, simulated timestamps, request bytes and response bytes SHALL be identical on every server start.
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL record each traffic log entry's request and response bytes from what the private simulator actually received and sent, and SHALL decode them with the same decoder as the frame inspector.
6. IF the captured exchanges differ from the incident script (missing transaction, unexpected status, or final register value other than 950), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail startup with an error rather than serve a partial or invented log.
7. WHEN traffic log generation finishes, THE SYSTEM SHALL dispose the private write-enabled simulator and SHALL serve learner reads for `phantom-writer` from a separate read-only simulator whose register 100 holds the final value observed in the captured log.
8. WHEN a learner reads unit 5, FC03, address 100, quantity 1 with scale 0.1 through `POST /api/test`, THE SYSTEM SHALL return raw register 950 and engineering value 95.0 with `unit: "°C"`.
9. WHEN the learner opens the traffic log, THE SYSTEM SHALL return it from `GET /api/incident/phantom-writer/log` with, per entry: sequence number, simulated time, client label, transaction ID, unit ID, function code and name, decoded address and value(s), and the request and response frames in the Requirement 1 format.
10. THE SYSTEM SHALL label the traffic log as a simulated capture and SHALL state that Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity and the client label is capture metadata.
11. WHEN `POST /api/incident/answer` receives exactly `scenario_id`, `transaction_id` and `client`, THE SYSTEM SHALL return `verified: true` only if both the transaction ID and the client label match the unauthorized write.
12. WHEN the answer is verified, THE SYSTEM SHALL return observations that cite the evidence from the captured log (function code 06, unit ID, register address 100, old value 650, new value 950, simulated time and client label) and a `mitigations` list labeled as real-world guidance not verified by this simulation, covering: network segmentation into IEC 62443 zones and conduits, allow-listing write function codes on a gateway or industrial firewall, Modbus/TCP Security (TLS with certificate-based roles), and change logging with review.
13. IF the answer is not verified, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return `verified: false`, an empty `mitigations` list and an observation describing what the captured log shows for the submitted transaction ID (or that no such transaction exists), and SHALL NOT reveal the correct pair.
14. IF the answer payload has missing, extra or duplicate fields, a `scenario_id` that is not a security case, a `transaction_id` outside 0–65535, or a `client` that is not 1–32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return HTTP 400 with `{ "error": "..." }`.
15. WHEN a learner views the traffic log before a verified answer, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT mark any row as suspicious; WHEN the answer is verified, THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the offending row with the text "Unauthorized write" and an icon in addition to color, and the row SHALL be reachable by keyboard.

### Requirement 3: Categories, difficulty and case picker

**User Story:** As a learner, I want cases grouped by type and marked with difficulty, so that I can tell troubleshooting exercises from security investigations and choose where to start.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SYSTEM SHALL include `category` (`"troubleshooting"` or `"security"`) and `difficulty` (`"beginner"` or `"intermediate"`) in every entry returned by `GET /api/scenarios`.
2. THE SYSTEM SHALL assign category `troubleshooting` to `pressure-scaling`, `unit-id` and `register-addressing`, and category `security` to `phantom-writer`.
3. WHEN the case picker is rendered, THE SYSTEM SHALL group scenarios by category using labeled groups ("Troubleshooting", "Security incidents") and SHALL show each case's difficulty as text.
4. WHEN a `security` case is selected, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the traffic log panel and the answer form; WHEN a `troubleshooting` case is selected, THE SYSTEM SHALL hide them.

### Requirement 4: Property-based tests

# Requirements Document: ot-security-lab

## Introduction

This feature extends GhostWire from a three-case Modbus troubleshooting lab into an OT security and troubleshooting lab. It adds:

- a frame inspector that shows the actual Modbus TCP bytes of every simulated read;
- a defensive incident case, **Phantom Writer**, in which the learner finds an unauthorized FC06 write in a simulated captured traffic log;
- case categories and difficulty;
- property-based tests in the existing dependency-free harness;
- updated judge documentation for all four cases.

The existing cases (The Giant Pressure, The Silent Sensor, The Wrong Register) keep their behavior. Existing API fields keep their names, types and meaning. Every value shown to a learner comes from a simulator run on loopback. Nothing in this feature connects to physical equipment, lets a learner send a Modbus write, or claims anything about a real installation.

The steering files `.kiro/steering/{product,safety,tech,modbus-protocol,accessibility}.md` apply to every requirement below.

## Glossary

- **ADU**: Modbus TCP application data unit. The 7-byte MBAP header followed by the PDU.
- **MBAP header**: Modbus Application Protocol header: transaction ID (2 bytes), protocol ID (2), length (2), unit ID (1).
- **PDU**: Protocol data unit. Function code (1 byte) followed by function-specific data.
- **FC03 / FC04 / FC06**: Read Holding Registers / Read Input Registers / Write Single Register.
- **Frame**: The exact bytes of one ADU sent or received on a loopback TCP connection.
- **Frame inspector**: The "Wire evidence" panel and the `frames` field that expose frames and their decoded fields.
- **Learner read path**: `POST /api/test` and the `ModbusClient` code it calls.
- **Incident generator**: Server-side startup code that performs the scripted Phantom Writer exchanges against its own private simulator and records them.
- **Traffic log**: The simulated captured traffic produced by the incident generator.
- **Client label**: A simulated name (for example `HMI-01`) that the incident generator assigns to each of its own TCP connections. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity; the label is capture metadata.
- **Evidence categories**: `observations`, `possible_causes`, `training_hints`, `next_steps`, `verified`.
- **Property**: A statement that must hold for every generated input in a property-based test.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: Frame inspector

**User Story:** As a learner, I want to see the exact Modbus TCP bytes of each simulated read and what each byte means, so that I can check my request and the device's reply from wire evidence instead of from a summary.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN `POST /api/test` completes with status `response`, `exception` or `error`, THE SYSTEM SHALL include a `frames` array in the result containing one request frame and, if any response bytes were received, one response frame.
2. WHEN `POST /api/test` completes with status `timeout`, THE SYSTEM SHALL include only the request frame in `frames`.
3. IF the request bytes were not fully written to the socket (for example the loopback connection failed), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return an empty `frames` array and SHALL NOT show a request frame that was never transmitted.
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL represent each frame as `{ "direction": "request" | "response", "hex": string, "fields": [ { "name", "value", "bytes" } ], "decode_error": string | null }`, where `hex` is the uppercase, space-separated hexadecimal form of the bytes and `bytes` is `{ "offset": int, "length": int }` into that frame.
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL build `hex` from the byte arrays actually written to and read from the loopback socket, not by re-encoding the request settings.
6. WHEN a frame is decoded, THE SYSTEM SHALL list these fields in byte order: transaction ID, protocol ID, length, unit ID, function code, then for an FC03/FC04 request the start address and quantity; for an FC03/FC04 response the byte count and one field per register value; for an FC06 request or response the register address and register value; for an exception response the exception code.
7. IF a response frame cannot be fully decoded (wrong protocol ID, length outside 2–254, byte count mismatch or truncated data), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return the fields decoded so far and a non-null `decode_error` describing the first failure, and SHALL NOT throw.
8. WHEN a result is rendered, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the frames in a collapsible panel titled "Wire evidence", collapsed by default, labeled as simulated.
9. THE SYSTEM SHALL render each frame as a `<table>` with header cells for field name, bytes (hex, monospace) and decoded value, and SHALL define MBAP, PDU, unit ID and function code in plain language the first time the panel shows them.
10. WHEN a learner hovers over or moves keyboard focus to a field row, THE SYSTEM SHALL highlight the matching bytes in the frame's hex display and SHALL indicate the link in text (byte offset and length), not by color alone.
11. THE SYSTEM SHALL make the panel and every field row reachable and operable with the keyboard alone, and SHALL respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Requirement 2: Phantom Writer incident case

**User Story:** As a learner, I want to investigate a simulated unauthorized setpoint change from a captured traffic log, so that I can practice identifying a Modbus write from evidence and learn which real-world controls reduce that risk.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SYSTEM SHALL provide a scenario with id `phantom-writer`, title "Phantom Writer" and category `security`, whose simulated device is a boiler controller at unit ID 5 with holding register offset 100 holding the temperature setpoint at 0.1 °C per count, documented normal value 650 (65.0 °C).
2. WHEN the server starts, THE SYSTEM SHALL generate the traffic log by performing real Modbus TCP exchanges over loopback between the incident generator and a private, write-enabled simulator that no HTTP endpoint can reach.
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL produce a traffic log of 12 transactions: 11 FC03 reads of holding register 100 from client label `HMI-01`, and one FC06 write of value 950 to register 100 from a different client label, at a fixed position in the sequence.
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL make the traffic log deterministic: client labels, transaction IDs, simulated timestamps, request bytes and response bytes SHALL be identical on every server start.
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL record each traffic log entry's request and response bytes from what the private simulator actually received and sent, and SHALL decode them with the same decoder as the frame inspector.
6. IF the captured exchanges differ from the incident script (missing transaction, unexpected status, or final register value other than 950), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail startup with an error rather than serve a partial or invented log.
7. WHEN traffic log generation finishes, THE SYSTEM SHALL dispose the private write-enabled simulator and SHALL serve learner reads for `phantom-writer` from a separate read-only simulator whose register 100 holds the final value observed in the captured log.
8. WHEN a learner reads unit 5, FC03, address 100, quantity 1 with scale 0.1 through `POST /api/test`, THE SYSTEM SHALL return raw register 950 and engineering value 95.0 with `unit: "°C"`.
9. WHEN the learner opens the traffic log, THE SYSTEM SHALL return it from `GET /api/incident/phantom-writer/log` with, per entry: sequence number, simulated time, client label, transaction ID, unit ID, function code and name, decoded address and value(s), and the request and response frames in the Requirement 1 format.
10. THE SYSTEM SHALL label the traffic log as a simulated capture and SHALL state that Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity and the client label is capture metadata.
11. WHEN `POST /api/incident/answer` receives exactly `scenario_id`, `transaction_id` and `client`, THE SYSTEM SHALL return `verified: true` only if both the transaction ID and the client label match the unauthorized write.
12. WHEN the answer is verified, THE SYSTEM SHALL return observations that cite the evidence from the captured log (function code 06, unit ID, register address 100, old value 650, new value 950, simulated time and client label) and a `mitigations` list labeled as real-world guidance not verified by this simulation, covering: network segmentation into IEC 62443 zones and conduits, allow-listing write function codes on a gateway or industrial firewall, Modbus/TCP Security (TLS with certificate-based roles), and change logging with review.
13. IF the answer is not verified, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return `verified: false`, an empty `mitigations` list and an observation describing what the captured log shows for the submitted transaction ID (or that no such transaction exists), and SHALL NOT reveal the correct pair.
14. IF the answer payload has missing, extra or duplicate fields, a `scenario_id` that is not a security case, a `transaction_id` outside 0–65535, or a `client` that is not 1–32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return HTTP 400 with `{ "error": "..." }`.
15. WHEN a learner views the traffic log before a verified answer, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT mark any row as suspicious; WHEN the answer is verified, THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the offending row with the text "Unauthorized write" and an icon in addition to color, and the row SHALL be reachable by keyboard.

### Requirement 3: Categories, difficulty and case picker

**User Story:** As a learner, I want cases grouped by type and marked with difficulty, so that I can tell troubleshooting exercises from security investigations and choose where to start.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SYSTEM SHALL include `category` (`"troubleshooting"` or `"security"`) and `difficulty` (`"beginner"` or `"intermediate"`) in every entry returned by `GET /api/scenarios`.
2. THE SYSTEM SHALL assign category `troubleshooting` to `pressure-scaling`, `unit-id` and `register-addressing`, and category `security` to `phantom-writer`.
3. WHEN the case picker is rendered, THE SYSTEM SHALL group scenarios by category using labeled groups ("Troubleshooting", "Security incidents") and SHALL show each case's difficulty as text.
4. WHEN a `security` case is selected, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the traffic log panel and the answer form; WHEN a `troubleshooting` case is selected, THE SYSTEM SHALL hide them.

### Requirement 4: Property-based tests

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want property-based tests for the codec, the transport and the diagnosis rules, so that edge cases are checked across many generated inputs and any failure can be reproduced.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SYSTEM SHALL implement property-based tests inside `csharp/GhostWire.Tests/Program.cs` (or files in that project) with no NuGet package, using a small seeded pseudo-random generator implemented in the harness.
2. THE SYSTEM SHALL print the base seed before running properties, SHALL accept an override through the `GHOSTWIRE_PBT_SEED` environment variable, and WHEN a property fails SHALL print the property name, the seed, the case index and the failing input before exiting non-zero.
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL run each property for at least 200 generated cases.
4. THE SYSTEM SHALL check property (a): for random valid inputs, encoding then decoding FC03, FC04 and FC06 requests and responses (including exception responses) returns the original field values.
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL check property (b): for random byte arrays of length 0–300, the decoder returns a result with either no `decode_error` or a non-null `decode_error`, and never throws.
6. THE SYSTEM SHALL check property (c): for random valid read requests against a loopback simulator, the status is exactly one of `response`, `exception` or `timeout`, and for `response` the number of returned registers equals the requested quantity.
7. THE SYSTEM SHALL check property (d): for every scenario and random request with status `timeout`, the diagnosis returns `verified: false`, at least two possible causes, at least one cause that does not mention the unit ID, and no statement asserting a single certain cause.
8. THE SYSTEM SHALL check property (e): for random valid read requests, the `frames` hex equals the bytes the simulator recorded as received (request) and sent (response).
9. WHEN all checks pass, THE SYSTEM SHALL keep printing `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.`.

### Requirement 5: Safety boundaries

**User Story:** As the project owner, I want the new features to keep every existing safety boundary, so that the lab stays a loopback-only, read-only training tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT accept a host, port or URL in any request field, query string or path segment of any endpoint.
2. THE SYSTEM SHALL bind the HTTP server and every simulator, including the private incident simulator, to IPv4 loopback only.
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL keep `POST /api/test` limited to function codes 3 and 4, and `ModbusClient` SHALL refuse to build or send any other function code.
4. IF FC06 is sent to any learner-reachable simulator, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reply with exception code 01 and leave registers unchanged.
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL perform FC06 only in the incident generator at startup, only against its private simulator, and only with values from the fixed incident script.
6. WHEN an AI provider is configured, THE SYSTEM SHALL send it the structured evidence including `frames` (and, for answers, the evidence of the matched log entry), and THE SYSTEM SHALL compute `status`, `raw_registers`, `frames`, `verified` and `mitigations` before and independently of the provider call.

### Requirement 6: Documentation

| P-c | **Transport status partition.** For all valid read requests against a loopback simulator, status ∈ {response, exception, timeout}, and for response `Values.Length == quantity`. | Simulator: unit 9, FC03 map with registers 0–199, FC04 map with registers 0–49. Unit = 9 with probability 0.9, else random 1–247. fc ∈ {3,4}; address 0–260; quantity 1–min(125, 65536-address). | Status in the set (never `error`); response length equals quantity; status `response` iff unit matches and the range lies in the map; `exception` has code 02. Cases run in batches of 8 concurrently to bound the time spent in roughly 20 expected 300 ms timeouts. |
| P-d | **Timeout diagnosis is never certain.** For all scenarios and requests with a timeout result, the diagnosis does not claim a single cause. | Pick any of the four scenarios; random valid `TestRequest`; synthesized `ModbusResult("timeout", [], null, exchange)` | `Verified == false`; `PossibleCauses.Length >= 2`; at least one cause does not contain "unit ID"; no observation, cause or next step matches `(?<!not |n't |never )\b(proves?|proven|confirms?|confirmed|certainly|definitely|the cause is)\b` (case-insensitive). Pure function, no sockets. |
| P-e | **Frames are the wire bytes.** For all valid read requests, `frames[0].hex == Hex(recorder.Received)` and, when present, `frames[1].hex == Hex(recorder.Sent)`. | Same simulator and generator as P-c, with an `IExchangeRecorder` that stores exchanges keyed by remote port | Request hex matches what the simulator received; response hex matches what it sent; for timeouts the recorder's `Sent` is null and there is exactly one frame. Uses the same frame-building function as `TrainingService`. |

Expected runtime: P-a, P-b and P-d take milliseconds. P-c and P-e each perform 200 loopback exchanges. With about 10% mismatched units and 8-way batches, each should take a few seconds; the harness prints the elapsed time per property.

### Manual checks

- Keyboard only: Tab into Wire evidence, open it, move through field rows and confirm the byte highlight and the "bytes N–M" text; select a log row and submit an answer; confirm the "Unauthorized write" badge is reachable.
- Screen reader spot check of the status announcements.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` in browser dev tools.
- Print report includes the incident answer attempts.

Record what was actually checked in `docs/verification.md`.

## Safety Review Checklist

- No new code path takes a host, port or URL from a request. The `scenario_id` route value is matched against a fixed list.
- The private write-enabled simulator binds loopback, is never stored where a request handler can reach it, and is disposed before the server starts accepting HTTP requests.
- `ModbusClient` cannot send FC06; `/api/test` validation still rejects function codes other than 3 and 4.
- FC06 values come from `IncidentScript` constants only.
- Every learner-facing value (log entries, frames, register values) is decoded from captured simulator bytes.
- Mitigations are labeled real-world guidance not verified by this simulation.
- The `ot-security-reviewer` agent reviews the diff against `safety.md` before the feature is considered done.

</content>
</file>

<file name="csharp/GhostWire/Incident.cs" language="plaintext" >
<content>
using System.Buffers.Binary;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Sockets;

namespace GhostWire;

public sealed record IncidentStep(string Client, ushort TransactionId, int OffsetSeconds, byte Function, ushort Address, ushort QuantityOrValue);

public sealed record TrafficLogEntry(int sequence, string time, string client, int transaction_id, int unit_id, int function_code, string function_name,
                                     int address, ushort[] values, string status, IReadOnlyList<DecodedFrame> frames);
public sealed record TrafficLog(string scenario_id, bool simulated, string capture_note, IReadOnlyList<TrafficLogEntry> entries);

// Fixed Phantom Writer script. These are inputs to the private simulator, not claimed results:
// every value in the log is decoded from the bytes that simulator actually received and sent.
public static class IncidentScript
{
    public const string ScenarioId = "phantom-writer";
    public const byte Unit = 5;
    public const ushort Register = 100;
    public const ushort InitialSetpoint = 650;
    public const ushort WrittenValue = 950;
    public const string ReaderClient = "HMI-01";
    public const string WriterClient = "MAINT-LAPTOP-07";
    public const ushort WriteTransactionId = 1111;
    public static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = new(2026, 10, 31, 2, 13, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    public const string CaptureNote = "Simulated capture generated at server start from loopback exchanges with a private simulator. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity; client labels are capture metadata.";

    public static readonly IncidentStep[] PhantomWriter = BuildSteps();

    private static IncidentStep[] BuildSteps()
    {
        var steps = new List<IncidentStep>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) steps.Add(new(ReaderClient, (ushort)(i + 1), i * 5, 3, Register, 1));
        steps.Add(new(WriterClient, WriteTransactionId, 33, 6, Register, WrittenValue));
        int[] later = { 35, 40, 45, 50 };
        for (int i = 0; i < later.Length; i++) steps.Add(new(ReaderClient, (ushort)(8 + i), later[i], 3, Register, 1));
        return steps.ToArray();
    }
}

// Startup-only component. It is the only code that encodes and sends FC06, and only to its own private,
// loopback-bound simulator, which is disposed before this method returns.
public static class IncidentLogGenerator
{
    private sealed class Recorder : IExchangeRecorder
    {
        private readonly object gate = new();
        private readonly List<SimulatorExchange> items = new();
        public void Record(SimulatorExchange exchange) { lock (gate) items.Add(exchange); }
        public SimulatorExchange[] Items { get { lock (gate) return items.ToArray(); } }
    }

    public static async Task<(TrafficLog Log, ushort FinalSetpoint)> GenerateAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var recorder = new Recorder();
        var clientByPort = new Dictionary<int, string>();
        var script = IncidentScript.PhantomWriter;
        await using (var simulator = new ModbusSimulator(IncidentScript.Unit, new() { [3] = new() { [IncidentScript.Register] = IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint } }, allowWrites: true, recorder: recorder))
        {
            foreach (var step in script)
            {
                var request = step.Function == 6
                    ? ModbusCodec.EncodeWriteSingleRequest(step.TransactionId, IncidentScript.Unit, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue)
                    : ModbusCodec.EncodeReadRequest(step.TransactionId, IncidentScript.Unit, step.Function, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue);
                using var deadline = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
                deadline.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(300));
                using var tcp = new TcpClient();
                await tcp.ConnectAsync(IPAddress.Loopback, simulator.Port, deadline.Token);
                clientByPort[((IPEndPoint)tcp.Client.LocalEndPoint!).Port] = step.Client;
                using var stream = tcp.GetStream();
                await stream.WriteAsync(request, deadline.Token);
                var header = new byte[7];
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(header, deadline.Token);
                int length = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(header.AsSpan(4));
                if (length is < 2 or > 254) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: invalid reply length {length}");
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(new byte[length - 1], deadline.Token);
                // The simulator records the exchange and then closes the connection, so end-of-stream means
                // this step's recording is complete and the steps stay strictly ordered.
                if (await stream.ReadAsync(new byte[1], deadline.Token) != 0) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: unexpected extra reply bytes");
            }
        }

        var captured = recorder.Items;
        if (captured.Length != script.Length) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture has {captured.Length} exchanges, expected {script.Length}");
        var entries = new List<TrafficLogEntry>();
        for (int i = 0; i < script.Length; i++)
        {
            var step = script[i];
            var exchange = captured[i];
            if (!clientByPort.TryGetValue(exchange.RemotePort, out var client) || client != step.Client)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} does not match the connection opened for its step");
            if (exchange.Sent == null) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has no response");
            if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request, out var request, out var requestError) || request == null)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} request did not decode: {requestError}");
            if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, out var response, out var responseError) || response == null)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} response did not decode: {responseError}");
            if (request.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || response.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || request.Function != step.Function || response.Function != step.Function)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} differs from the script");
            ushort[] values = step.Function == 6 ? new[] { response.QuantityOrValue!.Value } : response.Registers;
            var frames = new List<DecodedFrame> { ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request), ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, request.Address) };
            entries.Add(new(i + 1, IncidentScript.Start.AddSeconds(step.OffsetSeconds).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), client,
                request.Header.TransactionId, request.Header.UnitId, request.Function, ModbusCodec.FunctionName(request.Function), request.Address!.Value, values, "response", frames));
        }

        // Validate the capture against the script: 650 before the write, an FC06 echo of 950, then 950.
        int writeIndex = Array.FindIndex(script, s => s.Function == 6);
        for (int i = 0; i < entries.Count; i++)
        {
            var e = entries[i];
            if (e.unit_id != IncidentScript.Unit || e.address != IncidentScript.Register || e.values.Length != 1)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has unexpected unit, address or values");
            ushort expected = i < writeIndex ? IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint : IncidentScript.WrittenValue;
            if (e.values[0] != expected) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} shows {e.values[0]}, expected {expected}");
            if (i == writeIndex && (e.function_code != 6 || !captured[i].Sent!.AsSpan(7).SequenceEqual(captured[i].Received.AsSpan(7))))
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture write is not an FC06 echo");
        }
        if (entries.Count(e => e.function_code == 6) != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture must contain exactly one write");
        ushort final = entries[^1].values[0];
        return (new TrafficLog(IncidentScript.ScenarioId, true, IncidentScript.CaptureNote, entries), final);
    }
}

using System.Buffers.Binary;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Sockets;

namespace GhostWire;

public sealed record IncidentStep(string Client, ushort TransactionId, int OffsetSeconds, byte Function, ushort Address, ushort QuantityOrValue);

public sealed record TrafficLogEntry(int sequence, string time, string client, int transaction_id, int unit_id, int function_code, string function_name,
                                     int address, ushort[] values, string status, IReadOnlyList<DecodedFrame> frames);
public sealed record TrafficLog(string scenario_id, bool simulated, string capture_note, IReadOnlyList<TrafficLogEntry> entries);

// Fixed Phantom Writer script. These are inputs to the private simulator, not claimed results:
// every value in the log is decoded from the bytes that simulator actually received and sent.
public static class IncidentScript
{
    public const string ScenarioId = "phantom-writer";
    public const byte Unit = 5;
    public const ushort Register = 100;
    public const ushort InitialSetpoint = 650;
    public const ushort WrittenValue = 950;
    public const string ReaderClient = "HMI-01";
    public const string WriterClient = "MAINT-LAPTOP-07";
    public const ushort WriteTransactionId = 1111;
    public static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = new(2026, 10, 31, 2, 13, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    public const string CaptureNote = "Simulated capture generated at server start from loopback exchanges with a private simulator. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity; client labels are capture metadata.";

    public static readonly IncidentStep[] PhantomWriter = BuildSteps();

    private static IncidentStep[] BuildSteps()
    {
        var steps = new List<IncidentStep>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) steps.Add(new(ReaderClient, (ushort)(i + 1), i * 5, 3, Register, 1));
        steps.Add(new(WriterClient, WriteTransactionId, 33, 6, Register, WrittenValue));
        int[] later = { 35, 40, 45, 50 };
        for (int i = 0; i < later.Length; i++) steps.Add(new(ReaderClient, (ushort)(8 + i), later[i], 3, Register, 1));
        return steps.ToArray();
    }
}

// Startup-only component. It is the only code that encodes and sends FC06, and only to its own private,
// loopback-bound simulator, which is disposed before this method returns.
public static class IncidentLogGenerator
{
    private sealed class Recorder : IExchangeRecorder
    {
        private readonly object gate = new();
        private readonly List<SimulatorExchange> items = new();
        public void Record(SimulatorExchange exchange) { lock (gate) items.Add(exchange); }
        public SimulatorExchange[] Items { get { lock (gate) return items.ToArray(); } }
    }

    public static async Task<(TrafficLog Log, ushort FinalSetpoint)> GenerateAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var recorder = new Recorder();
        var clientByPort = new Dictionary<int, string>();
        var script = IncidentScript.PhantomWriter;
        await using (var simulator = new ModbusSimulator(IncidentScript.Unit, new() { [3] = new() { [IncidentScript.Register] = IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint } }, allowWrites: true, recorder: recorder))
        {
            foreach (var step in script)
            {
                var request = step.Function == 6
                    ? ModbusCodec.EncodeWriteSingleRequest(step.TransactionId, IncidentScript.Unit, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue)
                    : ModbusCodec.EncodeReadRequest(step.TransactionId, IncidentScript.Unit, step.Function, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue);
                using var deadline = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
                deadline.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(300));
                using var tcp = new TcpClient();
                await tcp.ConnectAsync(IPAddress.Loopback, simulator.Port, deadline.Token);
                clientByPort[((IPEndPoint)tcp.Client.LocalEndPoint!).Port] = step.Client;
                using var stream = tcp.GetStream();
                await stream.WriteAsync(request, deadline.Token);
                var header = new byte[7];
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(header, deadline.Token);
                int length = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(header.AsSpan(4));
                if (length is < 2 or > 254) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: invalid reply length {length}");
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(new byte[length - 1], deadline.Token);
                // The simulator records the exchange and then closes the connection, so end-of-stream means
                // this step's recording is complete and the steps stay strictly ordered.
                if (await stream.ReadAsync(new byte[1], deadline.Token) != 0) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: unexpected extra reply bytes");
            }
        }

        var captured = recorder.Items;
        if (captured.Length != script.Length) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture has {captured.Length} exchanges, expected {script.Length}");
        var entries = new List<TrafficLogEntry>();
        for (int i = 0; i < script.Length; i++)
        {
            var step = script[i];
            var exchange = captured[i];
            if (!clientByPort.TryGetValue(exchange.RemotePort, out var client) || client != step.Client)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} does not match the connection opened for its step");
            if (exchange.Sent == null) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has no response");
            if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request, out var request, out var requestError) || request == null)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} request did not decode: {requestError}");
            if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, out var response, out var responseError) || response == null)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} response did not decode: {responseError}");
            if (request.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || response.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || request.Function != step.Function || response.Function != step.Function)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} differs from the script");
            ushort[] values = step.Function == 6 ? new[] { response.QuantityOrValue!.Value } : response.Registers;
            var frames = new List<DecodedFrame> { ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request), ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, request.Address) };
            entries.Add(new(i + 1, IncidentScript.Start.AddSeconds(step.OffsetSeconds).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), client,
                request.Header.TransactionId, request.Header.UnitId, request.Function, ModbusCodec.FunctionName(request.Function), request.Address!.Value, values, "response", frames));
        }

        // Validate the capture against the script: 650 before the write, an FC06 echo of 950, then 950.
        int writeIndex = Array.FindIndex(script, s => s.Function == 6);
        for (int i = 0; i < entries.Count; i++)
        {
            var e = entries[i];
            if (e.unit_id != IncidentScript.Unit || e.address != IncidentScript.Register || e.values.Length != 1)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has unexpected unit, address or values");
            ushort expected = i < writeIndex ? IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint : IncidentScript.WrittenValue;
            if (e.values[0] != expected) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} shows {e.values[0]}, expected {expected}");
            if (i == writeIndex && (e.function_code != 6 || !captured[i].Sent!.AsSpan(7).SequenceEqual(captured[i].Received.AsSpan(7))))
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture write is not an FC06 echo");
        }
        if (entries.Count(e => e.function_code == 6) != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture must contain exactly one write");
        ushort final = entries[^1].values[0];
        return (new TrafficLog(IncidentScript.ScenarioId, true, IncidentScript.CaptureNote, entries), final);
    }
}

using System.Globalization;
using System.Net.Http.Headers;
using System.Text;
using System.Text.Json;

namespace GhostWire;

public sealed record Setup(int unit_id, int function_code, int address, int quantity, double scale);
public sealed record TestRequest(string scenario_id, int unit_id, int function_code, int address, int quantity, double scale);
public sealed record AnswerRequest(string scenario_id, int transaction_id, string client);
public sealed record Scenario(string id, string title, string summary, Setup initial, string[] documentation, int unit, int function, int address, ushort value, double? requiredScale, string category, string difficulty, string? engineeringUnit);

public sealed class TrainingService : IAsyncDisposable
{
    private static readonly Scenario[] Cases = {
        new("pressure-scaling", "The Giant Pressure", "A pressure reading responds, but its engineering value looks wrong.", new(7,3,10,1,1), new[] { "Simulated device: unit 7, holding register offset 10.", "The simulated pressure register uses a multiplier of 0.01 bar per count." }, 7,3,10,39,0.01, "troubleshooting", "beginner", "bar"),
        new("unit-id", "The Silent Sensor", "A read times out despite a running simulated gateway.", new(1,4,0,1,1), new[] { "Simulated gateway routes this device at unit 17.", "The simulated device publishes its value at input register offset 0.", "In this simulation only, a unit mismatch is silently ignored." }, 17,4,0,73,null, "troubleshooting", "beginner", null),
        new("register-addressing", "The Wrong Register", "The device responds with an illegal data address exception.", new(3,4,21,1,1), new[] { "Simulated device: unit 3, input register offset 20.", "This exercise uses zero-based protocol offsets, not one-based register labels." }, 3,4,20,125,null, "troubleshooting", "intermediate", null),
        // The phantom-writer simulator is seeded from the captured final value, not from `value` (the documented normal setpoint).
        new(IncidentScript.ScenarioId, "Phantom Writer", "A simulated boiler setpoint changed without an approved work order.", new(5,3,100,1,0.1), new[] { "Simulated boiler controller: unit 5, holding register offset 100 is the temperature setpoint.", "The setpoint register uses 0.1 °C per count. The documented normal value is 650 (65.0 °C).", "A simulated traffic capture from the controller's network segment is available for this case." }, 5,3,100,IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint,0.1, "security", "intermediate", "°C")
    };
    private readonly Dictionary<string, ModbusSimulator> simulators = new();
    private readonly TrafficLog incidentLog;
    public static IReadOnlyList<Scenario> All => Cases;
    private static readonly HttpClient Provider = new(new HttpClientHandler { AllowAutoRedirect = false }) { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(4) };

    public TrainingService()
    {
        try
        {
            foreach (var item in Cases.Where(c => c.category != "security"))
                simulators.Add(item.id, new ModbusSimulator(item.unit, new() { [item.function] = new() { [item.address] = item.value } }));
            using var deadline = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
            var (log, finalSetpoint) = IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateAsync(deadline.Token).GetAwaiter().GetResult();
            incidentLog = log;
            // Learner-facing and read-only: FC06 sent here returns exception 01.
            simulators.Add(IncidentScript.ScenarioId, new ModbusSimulator(IncidentScript.Unit, new() { [3] = new() { [IncidentScript.Register] = finalSetpoint } }));
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            foreach (var sim in simulators.Values) sim.DisposeAsync().AsTask().GetAwaiter().GetResult();
            if (ex is OperationCanceledException) throw new InvalidOperationException("Phantom Writer traffic log generation exceeded its 5 s startup deadline", ex);
            throw;
        }
    }

    // For the harness only: the port of a learner-facing, read-only simulator. Never exposed over HTTP.
    public int SimulatorPort(string scenarioId) => simulators[scenarioId].Port;

    public object Scenarios() => new { scenarios = Cases.Select(c => new { c.id, c.title, c.summary, c.initial, c.documentation, c.category, c.difficulty }).ToArray() };

    public static TestRequest Validate(JsonElement payload)
    {
        string[] fields = { "scenario_id", "unit_id", "function_code", "address", "quantity", "scale" };
        if (payload.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) throw new ArgumentException("Expected exactly scenario_id, unit_id, function_code, address, quantity and scale");
        var names = payload.EnumerateObject().Select(p => p.Name).ToArray();
        if (names.Length != fields.Length || names.Distinct(StringComparer.Ordinal).Count() != fields.Length || names.Except(fields, StringComparer.Ordinal).Any())
            throw new ArgumentException("Expected exactly scenario_id, unit_id, function_code, address, quantity and scale");
        var scenario = payload.GetProperty("scenario_id");
        if (scenario.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String || !Cases.Any(c => c.id == scenario.GetString())) throw new ArgumentException("Unknown scenario_id");
        int Number(string name, int min, int max)
        {
            var n = payload.GetProperty(name);
            if (n.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Number || !n.TryGetInt32(out int v) || v < min || v > max) throw new ArgumentException($"{name} is outside its allowed range");
            return v;
        }
        int unit = Number("unit_id", 1, 247), function = Number("function_code", 3, 4), address = Number("address", 0, 65535), quantity = Number("quantity", 1, 125);
        if (address + quantity > 65536) throw new ArgumentException("Invalid function or register range");
        var scaleElement = payload.GetProperty("scale");
        if (scaleElement.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Number || !scaleElement.TryGetDouble(out double scale) || !double.IsFinite(scale) || scale <= 0 || scale > 1000000)
            throw new ArgumentException("scale must be finite, positive and at most 1000000");
        return new(scenario.GetString()!, unit, function, address, quantity, scale);
    }

    public async Task<Dictionary<string, object?>> TestAsync(TestRequest request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var scenario = Cases.Single(c => c.id == request.scenario_id);
        var response = await ModbusClient.ReadAsync(simulators[scenario.id].Port, request.unit_id, request.function_code, request.address, request.quantity, ct);
        double? value = response.Values.Length > 0 ? response.Values[0] * request.scale : null;
        var diagnosis = Diagnosis.ForRead(scenario, request, response, value);
        var observations = diagnosis.Observations;
        var steps = diagnosis.NextSteps;
        var result = new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["status"] = response.Status, ["raw_registers"] = response.Values, ["engineering_value"] = value, ["observations"] = observations, ["possible_causes"] = diagnosis.PossibleCauses, ["training_hints"] = diagnosis.TrainingHints, ["next_steps"] = steps, ["verified"] = diagnosis.Verified, ["request"] = request };
        if (scenario.engineeringUnit != null) result["unit"] = scenario.engineeringUnit;
        result["frames"] = BuildFrames(response.Exchange, request.address);
        var (explanation, source) = await ExplainAsync(result, observations, steps, ct);
        result["explanation"] = explanation; result["explanation_source"] = source;
        return result;
    }

    // Frames come from the bytes actually written and read on the loopback socket, never from re-encoding the settings.
    public static List<DecodedFrame> BuildFrames(ModbusExchange exchange, int requestAddress)
    {
        var frames = new List<DecodedFrame>();
        if (exchange.Sent == null) return frames;
        frames.Add(ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Request));
        if (exchange.Received != null)
        {
            var response = ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Response, requestAddress);
            // A client stop explains the short frame; the decoder alone would report it as a truncated simulator reply.
            frames.Add(exchange.ClientStop == null ? response : response with { decode_error = exchange.ClientStop });
        }
        return frames;
    }

    private static async Task<(string, string)> ExplainAsync(Dictionary<string, object?> evidence, List<string> observations, string[] steps, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        string fallback = "This is simulated training evidence. " + string.Join(" ", observations) + " " + string.Join(" ", steps);
        string? rawBase = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GHOSTWIRE_AI_BASE_URL")?.TrimEnd('/');
        string? key = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GHOSTWIRE_AI_API_KEY");
        string? model = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GHOSTWIRE_AI_MODEL");
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(rawBase) || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(key) || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(model) ||
            !Uri.TryCreate(rawBase, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) || (uri.Scheme != "http" && uri.Scheme != "https") || string.IsNullOrEmpty(uri.Host) || uri.UserInfo.Length != 0 || uri.Query.Length != 0 || uri.Fragment.Length != 0)
            return (fallback, "deterministic");
        try
        {
            using var deadline = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
            deadline.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(4));
            var body = new { model, messages = new[] { new { role = "system", content = "Explain this simulated Modbus training evidence concisely. Never claim real-device access. Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses; do not change or invent protocol results." }, new { role = "user", content = JsonSerializer.Serialize(evidence) } }, temperature = 0.2 };
            using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, rawBase + "/chat/completions");
            request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", key);
            request.Content = new StringContent(JsonSerializer.Serialize(body), Encoding.UTF8, "application/json");
            using var response = await Provider.SendAsync(request, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, deadline.Token);
            if (!response.IsSuccessStatusCode || response.Content.Headers.ContentLength > 65536) return (fallback, "deterministic");
            using var stream = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(deadline.Token);
            using var buffer = new MemoryStream();
            var chunk = new byte[4096];
            while (true)
            {
                int read = await stream.ReadAsync(chunk, deadline.Token);
                if (read == 0) break;
                if (buffer.Length + read > 65536) return (fallback, "deterministic");
                buffer.Write(chunk, 0, read);
            }
            using var document = JsonDocument.Parse(buffer.ToArray());
            var content = document.RootElement.GetProperty("choices")[0].GetProperty("message").GetProperty("content").GetString()?.Trim();
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(content)) return (content[..Math.Min(content.Length, 4000)], "openai-compatible");
        }
        catch (Exception ex) when (ex is HttpRequestException or IOException or TaskCanceledException or JsonException or InvalidOperationException or KeyNotFoundException or ArgumentException or FormatException or IndexOutOfRangeException) { }
        return (fallback, "deterministic");
    }

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() { foreach (var simulator in simulators.Values) await simulator.DisposeAsync(); }

    public static readonly string[] Mitigations = {
        "Real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation: segment the control network into IEC 62443 zones and conduits so only approved systems can reach the controller.",
        "Real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation: allow-list write function codes (such as FC06 and FC16) per source on a Modbus-aware gateway or industrial firewall.",
        "Real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation: where devices support it, use Modbus/TCP Security (TLS with X.509 certificates that carry roles) so writes require an authorized identity.",
        "Real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation: log setpoint changes with source and time, and review them against change records."
    };

    private static bool IsSecurityCase(string? id) => id != null && Cases.Any(c => c.category == "security" && c.id == id);

    // scenario_id is matched against the fixed list of security cases; it never builds a path, host or URL.
    public TrafficLog? IncidentLog(string scenarioId) => scenarioId == IncidentScript.ScenarioId ? incidentLog : null;

    public static AnswerRequest ValidateAnswer(JsonElement payload)
    {
        string[] fields = { "scenario_id", "transaction_id", "client" };
        const string shape = "Expected exactly scenario_id, transaction_id and client";
        if (payload.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) throw new ArgumentException(shape);
        var names = payload.EnumerateObject().Select(p => p.Name).ToArray();
        if (names.Length != fields.Length || names.Distinct(StringComparer.Ordinal).Count() != fields.Length || names.Except(fields, StringComparer.Ordinal).Any())
            throw new ArgumentException(shape);
        var scenario = payload.GetProperty("scenario_id");
        if (scenario.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String || !IsSecurityCase(scenario.GetString())) throw new ArgumentException("scenario_id must be a security case");
        var tx = payload.GetProperty("transaction_id");
        if (tx.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Number || !tx.TryGetInt32(out int transaction) || transaction is < 0 or > 65535) throw new ArgumentException("transaction_id is outside its allowed range");
        var clientElement = payload.GetProperty("client");
        string? client = clientElement.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.String ? clientElement.GetString() : null;
        if (client == null || !System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex.IsMatch(client, "^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,32}$")) throw new ArgumentException("client must be 1-32 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-'");
        return new(scenario.GetString()!, transaction, client);
    }

    public async Task<Dictionary<string, object?>> AnswerAsync(AnswerRequest answer, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var diagnosis = Diagnosis.ForAnswer(incidentLog, answer);
        var entry = incidentLog.entries.FirstOrDefault(e => e.transaction_id == answer.transaction_id);
        // An unverified answer must not reveal the writer's label, so the matched write entry is redacted.
        if (entry != null && !diagnosis.Verified && entry.function_code == 6) entry = entry with { client = "(not shown until the answer is verified)" };
        var result = new Dictionary<string, object?>
        {
            ["status"] = "answered", ["verified"] = diagnosis.Verified, ["answer"] = answer,
            ["observations"] = diagnosis.Observations, ["possible_causes"] = diagnosis.PossibleCauses, ["training_hints"] = diagnosis.TrainingHints,
            ["next_steps"] = diagnosis.NextSteps, ["mitigations"] = diagnosis.Verified ? Mitigations : Array.Empty<string>(), ["log_entry"] = entry
        };
        var (explanation, source) = await ExplainAsync(result, diagnosis.Observations, diagnosis.NextSteps, ct);
        result["explanation"] = explanation; result["explanation_source"] = source;
        return result;
    }
}

public sealed record DiagnosisResult(List<string> Observations, string[] PossibleCauses, string[] TrainingHints, string[] NextSteps, bool Verified);

// Pure diagnosis rules: no sockets, no provider. `Verified` is true only when deterministic rules confirm the
// expected scenario settings and a successful simulator response.
public static class Diagnosis
{
    public static DiagnosisResult ForRead(Scenario scenario, TestRequest request, ModbusResult response, double? value)
    {
        bool verified = response.Status == "response" && request.unit_id == scenario.unit && request.function_code == scenario.function && request.address == scenario.address && request.quantity == 1 && (!scenario.requiredScale.HasValue || request.scale == scenario.requiredScale.Value);
        var observations = new List<string> { $"Simulated request: unit ID {request.unit_id}, function {request.function_code}, address {request.address}, quantity {request.quantity}." };
        string[] causes, steps;
        if (response.Status == "response")
        {
            observations.Add($"Simulated FC{request.function_code:D2} response returned {response.Values.Length} register(s): [{string.Join(", ", response.Values)}].");
            observations.Add($"The first raw register multiplied by the selected scale is {value!.Value.ToString("G", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}.");
            causes = verified ? Array.Empty<string>() : new[] { "A successful read does not by itself confirm scaling, register choice or interpretation." };
            steps = verified ? new[] { "The expected scenario settings and a successful response are verified." } : new[] { "Compare the setting and interpreted value with the simulated device documentation." };
        }
        else if (response.Status == "timeout")
        {
            observations.Add("The simulated Modbus request timed out without a response.");
            causes = new[] { "A unit ID mismatch is one possible cause; timeouts alone do not prove it.", "A connection issue or unavailable device could also cause a timeout." };
            steps = new[] { "Compare the unit ID with the simulated gateway documentation and retest." };
        }
        else if (response.Status == "exception")
        {
            observations.Add($"The simulated device returned Modbus exception code {response.ExceptionCode:D2}.");

using System.Buffers.Binary;
using System.Globalization;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Sockets;

namespace GhostWire;

public sealed record SimulatorExchange(int RemotePort, byte[] Received, byte[]? Sent);
public interface IExchangeRecorder { void Record(SimulatorExchange exchange); }

public sealed class ModbusSimulator : IAsyncDisposable
{
    private readonly TcpListener listener = new(IPAddress.Loopback, 0);
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource stopping = new();
    private readonly SemaphoreSlim slots = new(32);
    private readonly int unit;
    private readonly Dictionary<int, Dictionary<int, ushort>> registers;
    private readonly bool allowWrites;
    private readonly IExchangeRecorder? recorder;
    private readonly object registerLock = new();
    private readonly Task acceptLoop;
    public int Port => ((IPEndPoint)listener.LocalEndpoint).Port;

    // allowWrites is true only for the private Phantom Writer simulator used by IncidentLogGenerator at startup.
    // Every learner-reachable simulator keeps the default and answers FC06 with exception 01.
    public ModbusSimulator(int unit, Dictionary<int, Dictionary<int, ushort>> registers, bool allowWrites = false, IExchangeRecorder? recorder = null)
    {
        this.unit = unit;
        this.registers = registers;
        this.allowWrites = allowWrites;
        this.recorder = recorder;
        listener.Start();
        acceptLoop = AcceptAsync();
    }

    private async Task AcceptAsync()
    {
        try
        {
            while (!stopping.IsCancellationRequested)
            {
                var client = await listener.AcceptTcpClientAsync(stopping.Token);
                if (!slots.Wait(0)) { client.Dispose(); continue; }
                _ = ServeAsync(client);
            }
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
        catch (Exception ex) when ((ex is SocketException or ObjectDisposedException) && stopping.IsCancellationRequested) { }
    }

    private async Task ServeAsync(TcpClient client)
    {
        try
        {
            using (client)
            using (var deadline = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(stopping.Token))
            {
                deadline.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1));
                var stream = client.GetStream();
                var header = new byte[7];
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(header, deadline.Token);
                int protocol = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(header.AsSpan(2));
                int length = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(header.AsSpan(4));
                if (protocol != 0 || length < 2 || length > 254) return;
                var pdu = new byte[length - 1];
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(pdu, deadline.Token);
                var received = header.Concat(pdu).ToArray();
                int remotePort = client.Client.RemoteEndPoint is IPEndPoint remote ? remote.Port : 0;
                if (header[6] != unit) { Record(remotePort, received, null); await Task.Delay(600, deadline.Token); return; }
                int function = pdu[0];
                byte[] reply;
                if (function == 6 && allowWrites)
                {
                    if (pdu.Length != 5) reply = new byte[] { 0x86, 3 };
                    else
                    {
                        int address = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(pdu.AsSpan(1));
                        ushort value = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(pdu.AsSpan(3));
                        bool written = false;
                        lock (registerLock)
                        {
                            if (registers.TryGetValue(3, out var holding) && holding.ContainsKey(address)) { holding[address] = value; written = true; }
                        }
                        reply = written ? (byte[])pdu.Clone() : new byte[] { 0x86, 2 };

            if (count != data.Length - 1) { error = $"Byte count {count} does not match the {data.Length - 1} data bytes present"; return; }
